title: Dangerous Goods Acceptance: loading, discharge and closure of an acceptance
content:
## Rule
Under the Dangerous Goods Acceptance product the voyage milestones of an acceptance are recorded by systems, not by the desk: an approved acceptance becomes loaded when the goods are loaded on board, loaded becomes discharged when the goods are discharged at the port of discharge, and discharged becomes closed when the acceptance file is closed. Discharge and closure are recorded by the vessel and terminal systems and never by the desk. Once goods are discharged no amendment, withdrawal or re-review is possible, and only payments, goodwill waivers of fees already booked and misdeclaration findings may still be recorded against the acceptance.

## After discharge — what may still be recorded
| Action on the acceptance | After discharge |
|---|---|
| Amendment of the declaration | not possible |
| Withdrawal | not possible |
| Re-review | not possible |
| Payment | may be recorded |
| Goodwill waiver of a fee already booked | may be recorded |
| Misdeclaration finding | may be recorded |

Nothing beyond the last three may be recorded against a discharged acceptance.

## Basis Q&A
- *Can the desk mark goods as discharged or close the file?* No; discharge and closure are recorded by the vessel and terminal systems.
- *Can a fee that was never booked be waived after discharge?* No; only waivers of fees already booked may still be recorded.
